The main provenance cautions that later stages must preserve are source-shape cautions rather than URL cautions: S025-S027 are course or promotional pages; S028 is one named casting professional’s process; S029 is a practitioner-shaped tone article; S030 is a client-facing hiring/script guide. citeturn2view0turn2view1turn2view2turn4view0turn5view1turn2view5

### 12. COMMERCIAL-SYN Readiness Decision

- **Is B4 complete?** Yes.
- **Did B4 add material evidence beyond B1/B2/B3?** Partial. It added bounded voiceover-style copy-analysis support and some generic screen-prep vocabulary, but not a new mainstream Commercial evidence layer. citeturn4view0turn4view1turn5view0turn6view0turn6view4
- **Did B4 provide enough evidence to reduce any prior limitation?** Partial. It slightly reduces the “voiceover-style Commercial” and “solo-copy / screen-prep vocabulary” limitations, but it does not materially reduce UGC/social, presenter-led or corporate/industrial uncertainty. citeturn2view3turn2view4turn2view5turn2view0turn2view1turn2view2
- **Did B4 create new caution areas?** Yes, partly. It sharpens the need to avoid importing course methods, practitioner tone taxonomies and client-side copywriting advice into scoring language. citeturn2view0turn2view1turn2view2turn5view1turn2view5
- **Is COMMERCIAL-SYN ready?** Yes.
- **Which remaining gaps must be carried into COMMERCIAL-SYN as explicit limitations?** UGC/social-style Commercial, presenter-led product, corporate/industrial Commercial, direct operational guidance for direct-address subtypes beyond B1/B2, explicit no-brief brand/product invention wording, and stronger non-inferential appearance/marketability exclusions beyond B3’s fairness spine.
- **Which B4 sources should be used only as conditional or low-confidence support?** All six, but especially S025-S027 and S030. S028 is the most usable conditional source; S029 is illustrative only.
- **Which B4 sources should be ignored or treated as out of scope if their evidence is too weak?** Any attempted UGC/social, presenter-led or corporate/industrial inference from S025-S030 should be treated as out of scope for synthesis, because the pages do not explicitly support those subtypes. citeturn2view0turn2view1turn2view2turn2view3turn2view4turn2view5

## Reusable handoff pack

### 13. Reusable Handoff Pack for COMMERCIAL-SYN

#### COMMERCIAL-B4 handoff summary

COMMERCIAL-B4 is complete and confirms that the conditional source set should remain exactly that: conditional gap-fill, not a new core evidence layer. The batch adds some genuinely useful material, but almost all of it is narrow and source-shaped. The clearest addition comes from COMMERCIAL-S028, which gives a usable voiceover-style method for analysing supplied copy: performance tone can be grounded in visual cues, written descriptors, product category, cue words and an identifiable point of view. That materially helps with one of the thinner areas left after B1-B3, namely spoken-copy or voiceover-style Commercial work. COMMERCIAL-S029 adds a secondary, much weaker layer by mapping voiceover tones to product types, but the source itself says the list is not comprehensive, so it should function only as illustrative shorthand rather than as a stable category system. COMMERCIAL-S030 adds low-confidence support from the client side: commercial voiceover scripts are built around brand, message, target audience, spoken-word readability and concise delivery, which may help later synthesis explain why some copy sounds natural and some sounds over-written. That said, S030 is a hiring guide, not a performer-assessment source. citeturn4view0turn4view1turn5view1turn7view0turn7view3

The screen-training pages add far less. COMMERCIAL-S025, COMMERCIAL-S026 and COMMERCIAL-S027 do support stage-to-screen adjustment, independent self-taping, solo preparation, screen confidence, professional audition practice and taking direction on and off camera. However, they remain generic training pages rather than Commercial evidence. They do not meaningfully solve UGC/social-style Commercial, presenter-led product, corporate/industrial or any concrete subtype logic. They are best kept as low-confidence vocabulary support only. citeturn2view0turn2view1turn2view2turn6view3turn6view4

Overall, B4 slightly reduces the prior limitations around voiceover-style Commercial and solo-copy / screen-prep language, but it does not change the larger synthesis picture. The strongest Commercial branch still rests on B1 distinctiveness, B3 fairness/access boundaries and B2 assessability. B4 should therefore be treated as optional, conditional support. COMMERCIAL-SYN remains ready, and the remaining subtype gaps should stay explicit limitations unless stronger future evidence is added. citeturn2view3turn2view4turn2view5turn2view0turn2view1turn2view2

#### Compact provisional findings list

- **COMMERCIAL-B4-F01** — B4 adds meaningful but narrow support for voiceover-style Commercial copy analysis through product cues, visual cues, cue words and point of view.
- **COMMERCIAL-B4-F02** — B4 adds low-confidence, product-linked tone-family language for commercial voiceover, but those tone families are explicitly non-comprehensive and must not become universal categories.
- **COMMERCIAL-B4-F03** — B4 adds low-confidence client-side support for conversational, concise, audience-aware spoken commercial copy, but this remains copywriting guidance rather than performer scoring.
- **COMMERCIAL-B4-F04** — The formal training pages add only generic screen-transfer, solo-preparation and audition vocabulary; they do not create Commercial-specific subtype evidence.
- **COMMERCIAL-B4-F05** — B4 does not materially resolve UGC/social-style, presenter-led product or corporate/industrial Commercial gaps.
- **COMMERCIAL-B4-F06** — B4 should remain conditional gap-fill only; it refines a few lingering limitations but does not change COMMERCIAL-SYN readiness.

#### Compact unresolved-items list

- UGC / social-style Commercial remains unresolved.
- Presenter-led product remains unresolved.
- Corporate / industrial remains unresolved.
- No direct B4 source creates a robust direct-address / presenter subtype rule.
- No-brief brand / product / audience invention remains only indirectly bounded here.
- Marketability / bookability / appearance exclusion remains primarily a B3 matter.
- Cross-branch leakage risk remains high if course-shaped or voiceover-shaped language is overused.

| Total B4 rows | 6 |

#### COMMERCIAL-B4 extraction limitations

- All six B4 sources are lower-authority than the B1-B3 corpus for Commercial assessment purposes.
- Three sources are course or promotional pages; one is client-facing; two are practitioner/platform-shaped.
- Voiceover-style support is real but narrow.
- Course-shaped screen-prep language remains too adjacent to define Commercial subtypes.
- No B4 source materially solves UGC/social, presenter-led product or corporate/industrial.
- Some B4 language increases caution rather than clarity, especially tone lists, audience targeting and desirability-coded examples.

#### What B4 added

- Narrow but useful voiceover-style Commercial copy-analysis support.
- Some point-of-view and product-cue language.
- Some low-confidence solo-copy / solo-prep / stage-to-screen vocabulary.

#### What B4 did not solve

- UGC/social-style Commercial
- Presenter-led product
- Corporate / industrial
- Stronger direct-address subtype logic
- Explicit no-brief invention rules
- Stronger explicit anti-marketability clauses

#### What remains as synthesis limitations

- Thin subtype support beyond mainstream screen-style Commercial
- Voiceover-style support remains conditional, not branch-defining
- No direct B4 authority for live-room inference
- B4 should not outrank B1, B2 or B3 in synthesis weighting

**COMMERCIAL-SYN readiness statement:** COMMERCIAL-SYN is ready. B4 may be cited conditionally where it genuinely helps voiceover-style or solo-preparation edge cases, but it does not alter the core synthesis base already established by B1-B3 and reinforced by B2.

**COMMERCIAL-B4 extraction complete. COMMERCIAL-SYN remains ready; B4 evidence should be treated as conditional gap-fill only.**

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 16. Reusable Handoff Pack for Next Stage\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 COMMERCIAL-OUTPUT-SPEC is complete. The Commercial branch has now been converted from approved revised baseline wording into a concrete output-specificity standard, preserved non-regression test map, adversarial scenario pack and display-layer verification checklist. No live Commercial reports, JSONs, screenshots or comparison-page examples were supplied, so this is not live-output QA and does not verify production rendering. It is a synthetic/adversarial map designed to support implementation planning and later live Commercial output QA.\
The output-specificity rule set contains COMMERCIAL-OS-R01\'96R21. The most important rules are Commercial distinctiveness, acting-as-presence/naturalism semantics, generic praise suppression, tone/copy/product grounding, no-brief grounding, task-specific camera and eyeline handling, assessability as a precondition, audio reliability, simple capture / anti-polish, process-only reader/admin/deadline boundaries, live-room-only overclaim boundaries, accessibility-safe non-deficit language, anti-marketability / anti-appearance exclusion, professional_presentation boundaries and display-layer verification.\
The test set maps COMMERCIAL-AUDIT-T01\'96T30 into COMMERCIAL-OS-T01\'96T30, with one additional safety test COMMERCIAL-OS-T31 for nudity / stunt / privacy / consent boundaries. Highest-priority tests are direct-to-camera Commercial, off-camera-reader Commercial, no-brief Commercial, supplied brand/product/copy, generic \'93natural/confident\'94 wording, poor lighting/framing, poor audio, assessable home capture, high polish with weak performance, paid/basic reader, response-to-direction overclaim, callback-readiness overclaim, no-brief brand/product/audience invention, marketability/bookability/look language, access-adapted context, speech/accent/gender-diverse voice safety, production polish in professional_presentation and timestamp underproduction.\
Residual limitations are COMMERCIAL-OS-I01\'96I15. The major limitations are no live outputs, unverified frontend/comparison/rendering behaviour, under-evidenced UGC/social, presenter-led and corporate/industrial subtypes, conditional-only voiceover support, partly inferential anti-marketability evidence and broad access detail for accent, speech difference and gender-diverse voice.\
Evidence basis: COMMERCIAL-S001\'96S030, COMMERCIAL-B1-F01\'96F09, COMMERCIAL-B2-F01\'96F09, COMMERCIAL-B3-F01\'96F10, COMMERCIAL-B4-F01\'96F06, COMMERCIAL-SYN-F01\'96F24, COMMERCIAL-AUDIT-I01\'96I17, COMMERCIAL-AUDIT-R01\'96R21, COMMERCIAL-REV-C01\'96C21, COMMERCIAL-REV-S01\'96S21, COMMERCIAL-FINAL-D01 and COMMERCIAL-FINAL-D02.\
What was testable: revised baseline wording, rule derivation, claim-scope restrictions, generic phrase suppression, adversarial test logic and preserved baseline constraints.\
What was not testable: live Commercial report quality, Commercial JSON/report-object behaviour, frontend labels, comparison-page labels, renderer/export timestamp parity and score-stability behaviour.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\cf0 Commercial performance claims should be strongest only when the tape is assessable: the performer can be clearly seen and heard, framing is task-appropriate, eyeline/reader setup is readable, lighting allows facial or physical communication to register, and continuity is sufficient to judge the performance. If visibility, framing, sound or continuity materially limits assessment, narrow the claims and lower feedback reliability rather than substituting generic performance criticism.\cell \row

\pard\intbl\itap1\pardeftab720\partightenfactor0
\cf0 Audio comments should distinguish audibility from Commercial performance. Poor sound, room noise, low volume, distortion or unclear capture may limit reliability, but they do not by themselves prove weak copy handling, weak naturalism or weak speech skill. Where spoken copy is audible enough to assess, comments may address clarity, pace, emphasis, rhythm, cue-word handling and tone. Do not treat accent, speech difference, gender-diverse voice, hearing difference or communication support as a Commercial deficit.\cell \row

\cf0 \strokec2 Commercial feedback must not become theatre-style acting feedback or generic screen-acting feedback. Avoid defaulting to theatrical stakes, extended character psychology, generic \'93screen naturalism\'94 or vague \'93presence\'94 language unless the task or tape supports that context.\
Commercial tone and copy feedback must be grounded in supplied brief, script, product, campaign, situation, visible copy clues or observable tape behaviour. If no brief or material context is supplied, do not invent brand, product, buyer, target audience, campaign world, product category, casting fit, commercial market, hidden brief requirement or platform requirement.\
Direct-to-camera, off-camera-reader, scene-style, no-dialogue and voiceover-style Commercial tasks require different evidence expectations. Use the most specific Commercial context supported by the brief or tape. If the context is unclear, say so and keep the report to observable Commercial evidence.\
Assessability is a precondition for reliable Commercial feedback. Strong Commercial performance claims require clear sight, audible speech or copy, task-appropriate framing, readable eyeline or reader setup, and enough continuity to judge the work. If technical or audio limitations materially reduce assessability, narrow the claim and lower reliability rather than converting those limitations into performance criticism.\
Simple domestic capture, phones, plain backgrounds and low-fuss setups may be fully acceptable if the performance evidence is readable. Expensive equipment, studio polish, paid editing, professional packaging, paid readers, paid coaching, wardrobe cost, home quality and production value must not become Commercial merit.\
Commercial reports must not use marketability, bookability, buyer fit, brand fit, target-audience fit, commercial look, appearance, body type, charm, charisma, class-coded polish, fame, follower count, social-media profile or protected characteristics as scoring evidence.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Add the following Commercial-specific guardrails:\
\pard\tx220\tx720\pardeftab720\li720\fi-720\sa240\partightenfactor0
\ls9\ilvl0\cf0 \kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Do not reward production polish, studio quality, expensive equipment, paid reader access, paid coaching, paid editing or professional setup access as Commercial merit.\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Do not penalise simple domestic capture if the tape is assessable.\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Do not treat reader quality, reader absence, upload friction, file naming, slate, early submission, fast turnaround or platform cost as talent evidence.\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Do not infer response to direction, callback readiness, live-room flexibility, campaign-pressure professionalism or client-room behaviour from a finished tape unless directly shown.\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Do not use voiceover-style evidence as a general rule for all Commercial tapes.\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Do not overbuild UGC/social, presenter-led product or corporate/industrial rules from the current evidence base.\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Do not treat access needs, disability, neurodivergence, visual impairment, Deaf/disabled access, hearing difference, speech difference, accent, gender-diverse voice, mobility difference, convalescence or adaptation as a Commercial deficit.\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Do not infer capability ceiling, professionalism, marketability, buyer fit or suitability from access context.\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Do not encourage unsafe, nude, stunt, intimate or privacy-compromising self-tape requests.\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Do not use protected-characteristic or stereotype-led suitability claims.\
\ls9\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0
\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Keep Commercial comments specific to this tape, this performer, this copy or task, this brief where supplied, and observable evidence.\

\outl0\strokewidth0 \strokec2 Direct-to-camera Commercial: lens relationship, addressee, immediacy, conversational scale, copy emphasis, tone, and product/situation grounding where supplied.\

\ls10\ilvl0\kerning1\expnd0\expndtw0 \outl0\strokewidth0 {\listtext	\uc0\u8226 	}\expnd0\expndtw0\kerning0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 \strokec2 14. Reusable Handoff Pack for COMMERCIAL-FINAL-AUDIT\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 COMMERCIAL-REV is complete at wording, evidence-standard and guardrail level. It preserves the current shared TapeCoach architecture, including the six score fields, current Commercial weights, caps, blockers, verdict thresholds, role-fit bounds, server-side recomputation, Step 1 / Step 2 pipeline, report schema, public JSON structure and Musical Theatre acting + song stabilised flow. No implementation, backend, schema, UI, weighting or score-field changes are proposed.\
The revision clarifies the current Commercial 
\f2\fs26 acting
\f1\fs24  field as Commercial presence / naturalism only where that meaning is grounded in observable Commercial evidence: copy communication, task-calibrated tone, believable scale, camera or reader relationship, addressee logic, rhythm, immediacy and product/situation grounding where supplied. It adds a clear distinctiveness guardrail so Commercial does not become theatre acting or generic screen acting by default. It also blocks no-brief invention of brand, product, buyer, target audience, campaign world, casting fit or platform requirements.\
The revision separates direct-to-camera work from off-camera-reader / scene-style Commercial work, adds conditional handling for no-dialogue / silent-vignette Commercial and voiceover-style copy, and explicitly carries UGC/social, presenter-led product and corporate/industrial as limitations rather than unsupported sub-rubrics. It codifies self-tape assessability as a precondition for reliable feedback, separates audio audibility from Commercial performance, protects simple domestic capture, and blocks production polish, studio quality, paid reader access, paid coaching and paid editing as Commercial merit.\
Fairness and safety were strengthened through non-deficit access handling, anti-marketability / anti-bookability / anti-appearance rules, protected-characteristic boundaries, and process-only handling for reader access, slate, upload, file naming, deadline pressure and self-tape burden. Live-room-only capacities such as response to direction, callback readiness and campaign-pressure professionalism are blocked unless directly shown.\
Compact change summary:\

}# Commercial S0 Source Census and Batch Plan

## Scope and method

This census was built to support the Commercial branch only. It does **not** rewrite the rubric, does **not** change the product architecture, and does **not** propose implementation. It identifies a lean, verified source universe for later extraction, with priority given to commercial casting guidance, self-tape guidance, union/professional process rules, and accessibility/fairness safeguards. The strongest public corpus is concentrated in materials from entity["organization","Equity","uk performers union"], entity["organization","SAG-AFTRA","us performers union"], entity["organization","The Casting Directors' Guild","uk ireland casting guild"], entity["organization","Spotlight","casting platform uk"], entity["organization","Casting Networks","casting platform us"] and entity["organization","Backstage","performing arts careers platform"], with lower-priority gap-fill material from entity["organization","London Academy of Music & Dramatic Art","drama school london"], entity["organization","Royal Academy of Dramatic Art","drama school london"] and entity["company","Voices.com","voice marketplace canada"]. citeturn14search2turn19view2turn20view3turn10search2turn18search2turn18search3turn8search15

Two patterns are already clear. First, there is a solid evidence base for **Commercial as a distinct performance context**: realism, tone calibration, camera relationship, copy handling, and simple, legible self-tape execution recur across named casting-director and platform guidance. Second, the strongest official guardrails are **process, fairness and access rules**: clear instructions, realistic timelines, no improper personal questions, no nudity in self-tapes, no paid-reader expectation, and judging performance rather than expensive equipment. citeturn0search1turn6search3turn0search7turn0search14turn0search8turn2view0turn3view1turn19view2turn20view1turn21view0

What is **not** strong at S0 is equally important. Public, high-authority guidance is still thin for UGC/social-style commercial work, presenter-led product video, and fully generalisable corporate/industrial descriptors. Searches in those areas surfaced mostly job-listing patterns or client-facing voiceover material rather than stable, audition-assessment guidance, so those areas should stay in the “gap-fill only / may defer” bucket until extraction confirms otherwise. citeturn13search10turn22search0turn23search20turn13search0turn22search8turn8search15

## Coverage analysis

The **highest-confidence extraction core** is B1 plus B3. B1 gives the clearest answer to the question “what makes Commercial meaningfully different from generic acting?”: multiple sources converge on realism, tone calibration, camera relationship, and direct-address or copy-handling choices rather than theatre-sized performance or vague “presence” language. B3 then places hard limits around what can and cannot be claimed: clear information, realistic self-tape burdens, no improper personal questioning, no nudity in self-tapes, no reader-payment expectation, access-led adjustments, and explicit separation between performance value and expensive setup. citeturn14search2turn6search1turn6search3turn0search7turn0search14turn0search8turn2view0turn19view2turn20view1turn21view0

B2 is also strong, but it is mostly **execution evidence**, not Commercial-specific theory. It is the right batch for assessability rules: framing, reader placement, eyeline, audibility, simple backgrounds, password-protected submissions and avoiding over-produced tapes. Those sources are essential for output-specificity later, but they should not be mistaken for commercial-performance scoring definitions on their own. citeturn15view2turn16view2turn16view3turn8search8turn8search5turn0search2turn14search3turn0search4

B4 is clearly **conditional**. It is useful if later extraction shows a genuine need to model voiceover-style commercial tasks, corporate/explainer copy or screen-training vocabulary, but these sources are thinner, more course-shaped, more client-facing, or more practitioner-shaped than the B1–B3 corpus. They are appropriate for carefully bounded descriptor support, not for primary scoring logic. citeturn18search2turn18search3turn22search8turn22search2turn8search15

One especially important negative finding already emerges from the official codes. None of the higher-authority materials support marketability, bookability, appearance, follower count, studio polish, charm, or class-coded presentation as valid performance evidence. The stronger official sources instead emphasise fair questioning, equal access, clear instructions, and judging performers on performance rather than equipment or irrelevant personal characteristics. citeturn3view1turn19view2turn20view1turn20view0turn16view0

## Lean extraction batch plan

| Batch | Included IDs | Purpose | Stop condition | Why this batch exists |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | COMMERCIAL-S001 to COMMERCIAL-S008 | Establish Commercial as a distinct assessment context | Stop when at least two source families converge on commercial distinctiveness, naturalism scale, direct-to-camera vs scene-style behaviour, tone handling and non-dialogue handling | Prevent Commercial from collapsing into theatre-acting or generic “presence” feedback |
| B2 | COMMERCIAL-S009 to COMMERCIAL-S014 | Lock assessability and self-tape execution rules | Stop when framing, eyeline, reader use, audibility, simple setup and anti-overproduction boundaries are all covered by multiple sources | Provides tape-visible evidence standards without changing architecture |
| B3 | COMMERCIAL-S015 to COMMERCIAL-S024 | Lock process, fairness, safety and accessibility boundaries | Stop when clear direction, realistic timing, no improper personal questioning, no-fee / no-paid-reader burdens, accommodation and no-nudity limits are fully covered | Prevents unsupported, biased or unsafe Commercial reporting |
| B4 | COMMERCIAL-S025 to COMMERCIAL-S030 | Fill only genuine gaps | Run only if B1–B3 leave unresolved questions around voiceover-style copy, corporate/explainer context or screen-training language | Avoids over-expanding into low-authority or off-scope material |

Recommended extraction order: **B1 → B3 → B2 → B4 (conditional)**. That order first defines what Commercial is, then fixes what Commercial may not overclaim, then grounds tape-visible execution, and only then fills any surviving gaps.

## Open questions and limitations

The source universe is strong enough to proceed, but several limits should remain explicit before extraction begins.

The first limitation is subtype coverage. Public, higher-confidence guidance is much stronger for **mainstream commercial casting and self-taping** than it is for UGC/social-style work, presenter-led product video, and broad corporate/industrial contexts. Searches in those areas turned up either job boards or client-facing material more often than stable assessment guidance, so those subtypes should not be overbuilt at audit stage unless B4 produces genuine convergence. citeturn13search10turn22search0turn23search20turn13search0turn23search31

The second limitation is source shape. Several useful Commercial-specific articles are still **named-expert or coach-shaped** rather than contractual or standards-based. They are valuable because they name observable behaviours, but they must be triangulated rather than imported directly into rubric language. citeturn6search1turn6search3turn0search8turn22search8

The third limitation is cross-branch risk. Some self-tape and screen-performance guidance is generic enough that it could leak into Acting or Voice if applied carelessly. Later extraction and synthesis will need to keep Commercial-specific camera relationship, copy communication and no-brief brand/product constraints scoped to Commercial only. citeturn15view2turn16view3turn8search8turn22search8

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 17. Reusable Handoff Pack for COMMERCIAL-AUDIT\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\fs28 \cf0 COMMERCIAL-SYN handoff summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 COMMERCIAL-SYN is complete and establishes a source-grounded evidence base for auditing the current Commercial baseline. The strongest finding is that Commercial should not be treated as theatre acting or as generic screen acting. The B1 evidence supports Commercial as a distinct performance context centred on believable, relatable and grounded reality; task-calibrated tone; copy handling; and camera relationship. Direct-to-camera and off-camera-reader setups need different evidence expectations, and no-dialogue / silent-vignette Commercial work is a real but thinner sub-context.\
The B2 evidence supplies the self-tape assessability layer. Finished-tape Commercial feedback is only trustworthy when the performer can be clearly seen and heard, framing is task-appropriate, eyeline is controlled, the reader setup is legible, and the tape is continuous enough to judge the work. This batch strongly supports a separation between technical assessability and Commercial performance quality. Domestic capture, phones and simple setups can be acceptable; expensive equipment, studio polish, editing and professional packaging must not become Commercial merit.\
The B3 evidence gives the official fairness, safety and claim-scope boundary. Commercial audition requests should give enough information to ground task claims, self-tape burden should be proportionate, paid-reader or fee-based platform access should not become a hidden requirement, and nudity, stunt, privacy and consent boundaries are strong. Protected-characteristic and stereotype-led suitability claims are tightly constrained. Accessibility-safe Commercial assessment must treat access needs, visual impairment, Deaf/disabled access, fatigue, lighting, time-slot issues, accessible materials and reasonable adjustments as process and fairness matters, not deficits.\
B4 remains conditional only. It adds useful but narrow support for voiceover-style copy analysis through product cues, visual cues, cue words and point of view, but it does not solve UGC/social-style, presenter-led product or corporate/industrial Commercial subtypes. It should not outrank B1, B2 or B3.\
No audit recommendations have been created yet.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 7. Topic-by-Topic Final Audit Summary\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\fs28 \cf0 Commercial distinctiveness from theatre acting\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. The revised baseline explicitly blocks theatre-acting default language and redirects feedback to Commercial copy, addressee, tone and task scale. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Commercial distinctiveness from generic screen acting\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. The revised baseline distinguishes Commercial from generic screen acting where copy, product, campaign and situation context matter. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Acting-as-presence/naturalism field semantics\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass with limitation. The wording clarifies Commercial 
\f2\fs26 acting
\f1\fs24  as observable presence/naturalism without renaming the field. Structural field-sharing remains a limitation, not a blocker.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Generic \'93natural / confident / presence\'94 suppression\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. The revised text names risky phrases and requires behavioural replacement evidence. Output enforcement remains live-QA dependent.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Tone calibration\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Tone must be grounded in brief, copy, product, situation or observable tape evidence. No revision loop required.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Copy handling\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Copy communication, cue-word handling, rhythm and point of view are now named as Commercial evidence where supported. Voiceover use remains conditional.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Product / brand / situation grounding\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. The revised baseline blocks unsupported product/brand/audience invention and allows grounding only where supplied or visible.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Direct-to-camera handling\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Direct address and lens relationship are task-specific. No universal direct-to-camera rule is introduced.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Off-camera-reader / reader-scene handling\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Reader-scene work is treated as mediated; reader access remains process rather than talent evidence.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 No-dialogue / silent-vignette Commercial\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass with limitation. The revision handles no-dialogue work conditionally and does not generalise it.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Voiceover-style Commercial as conditional\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass with limitation. Voiceover-style evidence is explicitly conditional and low-confidence relative to B1\'96B3.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 UGC / social-style limitation\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. The revision keeps UGC/social-style as a limitation, not a universal Commercial subtype.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Presenter-led product limitation\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Presenter-led product remains under-evidenced and safely constrained.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Corporate / industrial limitation\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Corporate/industrial remains an explicit limitation.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 No-brief brand / product / situation invention\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. No-brief Commercial reports are restricted to observable evidence. This is a critical non-regression target.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Technical assessability versus performance\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Assessability is a precondition and limited sight/sound narrows reliability before performance criticism.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Audio / speech audibility\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Poor audio does not prove weak Commercial performance or weak speech skill.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Simple capture / anti-polish\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Domestic capture and phones are protected; studio polish and production value are blocked as merit.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Equipment / production-value exclusion\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Expensive equipment, studio polish, paid coaching and paid editing are excluded as talent evidence.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Reader-as-process support\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Reader access, quality and paid-resource status are process issues.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Self-tape burden, upload and deadline process boundaries\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Early submission, upload friction, file naming and deadline pressure are bounded as process/admin.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 professional_presentation boundaries\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. professional_presentation is limited to assessability, brief response, safe process and observable task preparation.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 brief_adherence / professional standards boundaries\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Explicit brief compliance remains possible, but no-brief invention is blocked.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Live-room-only / process-only overclaim\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Direction response, callback readiness and client-room behaviour are blocked unless directly shown.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Callback readiness and response-to-direction scope\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Finished tape evidence cannot prove these capacities unless explicitly present.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Nudity / stunt / privacy / consent boundaries\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. These remain safety/process issues, not performer merit or willingness.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Accessibility-safe and non-deficit handling\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass with limitation. Strong non-deficit rule added; accent, speech difference and gender-diverse voice detail remains broad.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Protected-characteristic and stereotype-led suitability boundaries\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. The revision blocks protected-trait and stereotype-led suitability claims.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Marketability / bookability / appearance exclusion\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass with limitation. The exclusion is strong enough for wording-level approval; some support is inferential rather than verbatim Commercial-specific.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Methodology / practitioner / source-shape overreach\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass. Source-shape caution is explicit and B4 is correctly conditional.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Display / label / comparison risks\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: accepted with limitation. Display behaviour remains unverified and is correctly carried forward.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa280\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs28 \cf0 Timestamp and next-take specificity\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Status: pass with limitation. Commercial-specific timestamp and next-take anchors are now present; renderer/export behaviour remains unverified.\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa298\partightenfactor0

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 13. Reusable Handoff Pack for COMMERCIAL-OUTPUT-SPEC\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 COMMERCIAL-FINAL-AUDIT is complete. The COMMERCIAL-REV package is approved with explicit limitations and is ready for Commercial Output Specificity / Non-Regression Test Mapping. The revision remains inside the live TapeCoach shared architecture and does not propose any score-field, weighting, cap, blocker, verdict-threshold, role-fit, schema, backend, pipeline, report-schema or UI implementation changes.\
The strongest accepted changes are COMMERCIAL-REV-C01 to C06 and C10 to C18. These clarify Commercial distinctiveness, 
\f2\fs26 acting
\f1\fs24  as Commercial presence/naturalism, copy/tone/product grounding, no-brief restraint, task-specific camera handling, assessability, audio reliability, anti-polish, process-only reader/admin/deadline boundaries, live-room claim limits, safety, accessibility, anti-marketability and professional_presentation. COMMERCIAL-REV-C03 and C20 also provide strong anti-generic and timestamp/next-take specificity rules.\
Accepted with limitation: COMMERCIAL-REV-C07, C08, C09, C16, C20 and C21. The limitations are evidence or verification limits, not revision blockers. No-dialogue evidence is thinner than mainstream Commercial evidence. Voiceover-style evidence is conditional and comes mainly from B4. UGC/social, presenter-led and corporate/industrial subtypes remain under-evidenced. Accessibility detail for accent, speech difference and gender-diverse voice remains broad. Display labels, comparison behaviour and renderer/export timestamp behaviour were not auditable.\
Final accepted section set: COMMERCIAL-REV-S01\'96S21, with limitations attached to S07, S08, S09, S16, S20 and S21.\
The next stage should convert the revised package into Commercial output-specificity rules, adversarial scenarios, display-layer checks and non-regression tests. Highest-priority output-spec scenarios are direct-to-camera Commercial, reader-scene Commercial, no-brief Commercial, supplied brand/product/copy, generic \'93natural/confident\'94 wording, poor lighting/framing, poor audio, simple home capture, high polish with weak performance, paid reader, response-to-direction overclaim, callback readiness overclaim, no-brief brand/product/audience invention, marketability/bookability/look language, access-adapted context, speech/accent/gender-diverse voice safety, production polish in professional_presentation, and timestamp underproduction.\
Evidence basis: COMMERCIAL-SYN-F01\'96F24, COMMERCIAL-AUDIT-I01\'96I17, COMMERCIAL-AUDIT-R01\'96R21, COMMERCIAL-REV-C01\'96C21, COMMERCIAL-REV-S01\'96S21, COMMERCIAL-S001\'96S030, COMMERCIAL-B1-F01\'96F09, COMMERCIAL-B2-F01\'96F09, COMMERCIAL-B3-F01\'96F10 and COMMERCIAL-B4-F01\'96F06.\
What was auditable: revised Commercial wording, audit recommendation response, synthesis compliance and baseline non-regression posture.\
What was not auditable: exact production prompt text, frontend labels, comparison-page labels, renderer/export timestamp behaviour, live Commercial output quality and implementation-layer subtype detection.\

\f0\b\fs36 \cf0 4. Branch Scope and Production Context\
\pard\pardeftab720\sa240\partightenfactor0

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 The Commercial branch covers TapeCoach\'92s operational 
\f2\fs26 commercial
\f1\fs24  audition type and its use of the shared six-field model, especially the 
\f2\fs26 acting
\f1\fs24  field as Commercial presence / naturalism. The completed Commercial refinement is intended to improve Commercial report specificity, field semantics, evidence anchoring, claim-scope control, self-tape assessability handling, professional presentation boundaries, accessibility-safe language and non-regression testing.\
The revised Commercial outputs are proposed branch improvements. They are not yet shipped production behaviour unless a later implementation and rollout explicitly applies them.\
Current live production behaviour remains separate from the research package. The live product continues to use the existing architecture, fields, weights, pipeline, schemas, scrubs and rendering system. This branch must not change those directly.\
Commercial must preserve:\

\cf0 Adversarial / non-regression tests: COMMERCIAL-OS-T01\'96T31 cover direct-to-camera, reader-scene, no-dialogue, no-brief, supplied copy/product, generic praise, mixed copy/camera evidence, poor lighting, poor audio, domestic capture, high polish/weak performance, reader resource, live-room overclaims, process/admin as talent, voiceover conditionality, unsupported subtypes, marketability/look language, access contexts, presentation polish, comparison mismatch, timestamp underproduction and safety/consent boundaries.\
Display-layer checks: Commercial category labels, 
\f2\fs26 acting
\f1\fs24  semantics, irrelevant Vocal suppression, component/category breakdown wording, comparison score/label parity, timestamp count/order/specificity, export parity, feedback reliability, professional_presentation wording, no-brief/role-fit display and risk flag wording.\
Accessibility / anti-bias protections: COMMERCIAL-OS-R16 and R17 must block access, disability, visual impairment, Deaf/disabled access, hearing difference, speech difference, accent, gender-diverse voice, mobility difference, convalescence, adaptation, appearance, body type, \'93look\'94, bookability and marketability as deficit or talent evidence.\
Timestamp expectations: COMMERCIAL-OS-R20 requires chronological, evidence-led timestamps tied to copy, camera, tone, physical/non-dialogue evidence or assessability, within the preserved maximum of 8.\

\f1\b0\fs24 \cf0 Commercial is mature enough for cross-branch consolidation. The branch is complete through source census, targeted extraction, synthesis, gap audit, revision, final audit, output-specificity mapping and implementation-readiness handoff. The stable ID families are COMMERCIAL-S001\'96S030, COMMERCIAL-B1-F01\'96F09, COMMERCIAL-B2-F01\'96F09, COMMERCIAL-B3-F01\'96F10, COMMERCIAL-B4-F01\'96F06, COMMERCIAL-SYN-F01\'96F24, COMMERCIAL-AUDIT-I01\'96I17, COMMERCIAL-AUDIT-R01\'96R21, COMMERCIAL-REV-C01\'96C21, COMMERCIAL-REV-S01\'96S21, COMMERCIAL-FINAL-D01\'96D02, COMMERCIAL-OS-R01\'96R21, COMMERCIAL-OS-T01\'96T31 and COMMERCIAL-OS-I01\'96I15.\
The strongest evidence base comes from B1, B2 and B3. B1 establishes Commercial as distinct from theatre acting and generic screen acting, with evidence around grounded reality, task-calibrated tone, copy handling and camera relationship. B2 establishes assessability and anti-polish: Commercial feedback is only reliable when the tape is readable, audible and task-appropriate, and simple domestic capture can be acceptable. B3 establishes the official process, fairness, safety and access spine: reader access, deadlines, upload burden, paid resources, nudity/stunt/privacy/consent, protected characteristics and accessibility must not become talent evidence. B4 is conditional only, mainly supporting narrow voiceover-style copy analysis.\
COMMERCIAL-AUDIT found the baseline directionally correct but too generic. COMMERCIAL-REV addressed this through wording and guardrail revisions only, preserving all score fields, weights, caps, blockers, verdict thresholds, role-fit bounds, schema, backend, pipeline, report schema and the MT acting + song anchor. COMMERCIAL-FINAL-AUDIT approved the revision with explicit limitations. COMMERCIAL-OUTPUT-SPEC created COMMERCIAL-OS-R01\'96R21 and COMMERCIAL-OS-T01\'96T31.\
Commercial is implementation-ready as a production-facing requirement package, not as shipped production behaviour. The key implementation-readiness implications are: clarify 
\f2\fs26 acting
